description: Graph-native figure/ground REGION GROUPING (jabberwock's design), replacing the Python recognised_figures/_components. Flood a connected-component label over the world's `neighbour` lattice (relax_to_fixpoint, no new primitive), then mint one Region per label via add_node_if_absent (dedup key=label), with `within` edges — so the existing figure_ground + shape_sense concepts run over real Regions.

microtheory.name: region_grouping
microtheory.description: cells + lattice -> connected-component labels -> one Region per component -> figure/ground.

attrs.question: How do you split a figure into components cheaply without re-flooding the whole floor every frame?
attrs.answer: Gate the low-order re-settle by HIGH-ORDER OWNERSHIP, not by 'a cell left'. The avatar is a high-order Body that OWNS its component Regions via the controls edge (a Region-of-Regions). A split re-flood runs over ONLY an owned Region's own members, triggered ONLY when an owned member leaves. The floor sheds a cell every frame too, but the floor is UNOWNED, so it never carries the resettle mark and is never re-flooded — O(body), not O(grid). The split rule copies the owner edge from parent to child (bd controls newregion), so 'which cells are the avatar' stays a 2-hop closure and a split figure is BOTH two low-order components AND one high-order body. The earlier ungated version hung: it re-flooded the 476-cell floor every step at O(floor^2). Ownership is the gate.

concepts.name: cc_relax_step
concepts.comment: flood: cc_label = min over same-value neighbours. relax_to_fixpoint drives it. DIRECT IfThenElse, FLOAT labels.

rules.name: prune_consumed_changes
rules.comment: Keep has_change at the current frame's ~6 edges: delete ChangeEvents from earlier frames (frame < game.frame). Current-frame CEs survive this tick (they drive membership) and are pruned next frame.
